alternatives: Ratify it now (rejected: nothing a person can see is rendered in the hosts our users run, so ratifying would accept sponsor bytes in an agent's context in exchange for revenue that cannot yet occur). Delete the record and the code (rejected: the mechanism is built, tested and constrained; the open question is only when a rendered slot is worth showing, and deleting the record would erase the reasoning that answers it). Mark the companion record superseded (rejected: it decides far more than placement - permanent exclusions for embed-server and the retrieval path, no ad containers, ad-free static exports, payload and label constraints - and superseding it retires all of that silently). Put it in result text so plain CLI hosts show it (rejected: that is the injection surface the payload constraints exist to close, and it makes sponsor copy part of what an agent reads as instructions).
consequences:
The REP-28 code stays merged and dormant: off for every install, inert without credentials, and now carrying no governance claim that it may be switched on. Enabling it needs this record ratified first, which is a human act via set_decision_status.

The active sponsorship surface is the viewer chrome chip the companion record authorizes, plus Ko-fi support. Anyone looking for sponsorship revenue should build that, not enable this.

Both records are live and neither supersedes the other. This one is deliberately NOT marked as superseding the companion record: its rulings on embed-server, the retrieval path, ad containers, ad-free static exports and the viewer chip all remain in force, and flipping it to superseded would retire protections nobody voted to retire. Read them together - the companion for what may never carry ads and what every payload must obey, this one for whether the MCP tool-result envelope may ever carry one.

The allowlist in mcp/src/ads/config.ts is the checkable form of the exclusions above: a change that puts semantic_find, a mutating tool, or an error path on it is a regression against a decision, not a feature, and so is any change that moves sponsored content out of the envelope into content or a manufactured structuredContent.

This record governs mcp/src/ads/, mcp/src/server/createMcpServer.ts and docs/SPONSORSHIP.md. It was created through the markdown import path, so it carries no graph anchors yet - a later session should anchor it with reaffirm_decision.
context:
REP-28 built the sponsorship mechanism as a slot on the MCP tool-result envelope: opt-in, disclosed, fail-open, fixed-schema, and off by default. The companion record adr:2026-08-21-sponsorship-placement-viewer-chip-only-deferred-to-rep-28-no (REP-30) named three surfaces and authorized one, a disclosed chip in viewer chrome. It said nothing about the MCP tool result, and it said a placement it did not authorize needs a new record rather than a quiet exception, so the implementer shipped the mechanism off and asked for a ruling.

The user's direction opening this epic was to develop a system for displaying ads inside the MCP, so the surface was in scope for REP-28 and the companion record's silence about it was a drafting gap rather than a refusal. That is why this record exists at all.

It is nonetheless recorded as PROPOSED and dormant: the ruling below is not to ratify now. An earlier draft of this record asserted ratification; that draft was wrong and is superseded by the text below, not by another record.
decided_by: claude (recording; motivated by Marcus's in-session direction "Add Lulu Ads monetization to my MCP server" — awaiting explicit human ratification via set_decision_status)
decision:
STATUS: PROPOSED, and deliberately dormant. This record authorizes nothing. Ratification is a human act via set_decision_status, and the standing ruling is NOT to ratify it now.

The reasoning: an envelope _meta field is machine-visible. A host that renders MCP Apps could show it to a person; the hosts our users actually run today, plain CLI agents, render it to nobody. That is the worst of both - zero revenue, since nothing a human could act on is displayed, and nonzero exposure, since sponsor-supplied bytes would still land in an agent's context on every eligible call. Revenue therefore routes through the surface the companion record already authorizes, the viewer chrome chip, plus Ko-fi support. The MCP slot stays built, tested and off.

Revisit trigger: MCP Apps rendering becoming common in the hosts RepoSkein's users run. When a rendered sponsored card would actually be seen by the person whose agent made the call, this record is worth ratifying. Until then it is not.

The terms that WOULD apply on ratification are already implemented and enforced by tests, so ratifying is a decision, not a build: envelope only, under a namespaced _meta key, never in result text, never an extra content block, and never a manufactured structuredContent; eligibility is an allowlist in code, not config, today exactly get_context_profile, with error results and mutating tools excluded; semantic_find and embed-server stay excluded permanently on every code path, per ruling 2 of the companion record; off by default, requiring no kill switch, an operator opt-in confirmed in the environment, both credentials in the environment only, and a non-supporter caller, and fail-open throughout; fixed-schema, length-capped payloads with an immutable sponsored label; and no sponsored data in .reposkein/ artifacts.

On this record's id: its slug says "ratified" because the first draft asserted ratification before this ruling. The slug is kept because ids are portable; status and this text govern.
title: MCP tool-result sponsored slot (proposed, deliberately dormant)
